en.p30Wrong132: 132 cm is the whole circumference. The arc is only one-third of it.
en.p31WrongS21: 21 cm is the radius. s is the arc, the length along the rim.

en.p32Right1: The blade length is the radius.
en.p32Right2: The sweep is the central angle.
en.p32WrongChord: The blade turns about one end, so it is a radius, not a chord.

en.p33Right2: The tip travels 44 cm in every sweep.
en.p33Wrong42: 42 cm is the blade itself, the radius. The tip travels a little further along the arc.
en.p33Wrong48: The whole circumference is 264 cm, and 60° is one-sixth of it: that is not 48 cm.
en.p34Ask: 45 minutes turns the hand through how many degrees?
en.p34Right: 45 minutes is three-quarters of an hour, so the hand turns three-quarters of 360°: 270°.
en.p34Wrong180: 180° is a half turn: the hand does that in 30 minutes, not 45.
en.p34Wrong45: The 45 is minutes, not degrees. The hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, so 45 minutes is far more than 45°.
en.p35Ask: How far does its tip travel in 45 minutes?
en.p35Right2: The tip travels 66 cm in 45 minutes.
en.p35Wrong88: 88 cm is the whole circumference: a full hour. In 45 minutes the tip travels three-quarters of it.
en.p35Wrong44: 44 cm is half the circumference: 30 minutes, not 45.

en.s4p5Start: Let's start with a circle and its centre.
en.s4p5Points: Mark two points on the circle.
en.s4p5Radii: Join each point to the centre with a radius.
en.s4p5Sector: The two radii and the arc enclose a minor sector.
en.s4p5Chord: Now join the two points with a chord.

en.s4p5Remove: Take the triangle away from the sector.
en.s4p5Left: What is left is the minor segment.
en.s4p6Summary: The segment is what the triangle leaves behind.

en.s4p7Ask: θ = 90°, so the triangle's area is …
en.s4p7Right: The two radii are the base and the height, so the area is {f}.
en.s4p7WrongHalfR: {f} has only one length in it. A triangle's area is ½ × base × height.
en.s4p7WrongRR: {f} is the area of a square on the radius. The triangle is only half of it.
en.s4p8AskSector: Choose the area of the sector.
en.s4p8AskTriangle: Choose the area of the triangle.
en.s4p8AskSegment: Choose the area of the segment.
en.s4p8Check: The segment must be smaller than the sector it was cut from. 56 cm² against 154 cm².
en.s4p8Wrong616: 616 cm² is the area of the whole circle. The sector is only a quarter of it.
en.s4p8Wrong77: 77 cm² is one-eighth of the circle. 90° is a quarter of 360°, not an eighth.
en.s4p8Wrong196: 196 cm² is 14 × 14, the whole square. The triangle is half of it.
en.s4p8Wrong49: 49 cm² is ½ × 7 × 14. Both sides of the triangle are 14 cm.
en.s4p8Wrong252: 252 cm² is 154 + 98. The triangle is taken away, not added.
en.s4p8Wrong46: 154 − 98 is not 46. Check the subtraction once more.
en.s4p9Ask: r = 7 cm and θ = 90°. Find the area of the minor segment.
en.s4p9Wrong38: 38.5 cm² is the area of the sector. The triangle still has to come off.
en.s4p9Wrong24: 24.5 cm² is the area of the triangle, the part that is taken away.
en.s4p10Ask: A sector is 154 cm² and its triangle is 98 cm². The segment is …
en.s4p10Wrong58: 154 − 98 is not 58. Take 98 from 154 once more: it leaves 56.
en.s4p11Big: Now the bigger piece: the major segment.
en.s4p11Back: It is the major sector with the triangle put back on.
en.s4p13AskSector: Choose the area of the major sector.
en.s4p13AskSegment: Choose the area of the major segment.
en.s4p13Check: Check it both ways: 56 + 560 = 616 = πr². The two segments tile the whole circle.
en.s4p13Wrong154: 154 cm² is the minor sector, a quarter of the circle. The major sector is the other three quarters.
en.s4p13Wrong616: 616 cm² is the whole circle. The major sector is 270° of the 360°.
en.s4p13Wrong364: 364 cm² is 462 − 98. For the major segment the triangle is put back on, not taken away.
en.s4p13Wrong462: 462 cm² is the major sector alone. The triangle still has to be added.
en.s4p14Ask: r = 7 cm and θ = 90°. Find the area of the major segment.
en.s4p14Right: Major sector 115.5 cm² + triangle 24.5 cm² = 140 cm². Or 154 − 14 = 140.
en.s4p14Wrong14: 14 cm² is the minor segment, the small piece. The major segment is the rest of the circle.
en.s4p14Wrong154: 154 cm² is the whole circle, πr². The minor segment still has to come off.
en.s4p15Pipe: A pipe of radius 14 cm lies on its side with water in it.
en.s4p15Subtends: The water surface subtends 90° at the centre.
en.s4p15Right: Sector 154 cm² − triangle 98 cm² = 56 cm² of water.
en.s4p15Wrong156: 156 cm² is more than the whole sector, 154 cm². The water is the sector less the triangle.
en.s4p15Wrong256: 256 cm² is more than the sector of 154 cm². The water is only a part of that sector.
en.s4p16Bed: A round flower bed of radius 21 m is cut by a straight path.
en.s4p16Subtends: The path subtends 90° at the centre.
en.s4p16Ask: How big is the smaller piece?
en.s4p16Right: Sector 346.5 m² − triangle 220.5 m² = 126 m². The bigger piece is 1386 − 126 = 1260 m².
en.s4p16Wrong252: 252 m² is twice 126. The smaller piece is the sector 346.5 m² less the triangle 220.5 m².
en.s4p16Wrong58: 58 m² is far too small for a radius of 21 m. The sector alone is 346.5 m².

en.s3PickAsk: Tap the card where the highlighted part is a sector.
en.s3PickWrongSeg: This is a segment. A segment is the region enclosed by a chord and an arc.
en.s3PickWrongArc: This is an arc. An arc is a part of the circle’s boundary, not a region.
en.s3PickRight: A sector is the region enclosed by two radii and the arc between them.
en.s3PickRecap: A segment is cut by a chord, a sector by two radii, and an arc is just a part of the circle.
en.s3NameAsk: Drag each name to the box for its sector.
en.s3NameWrongMinor: Look again! This box points to the smaller region.
en.s3NameWrongMajor: Look again! This box points to the larger region.

en.s3ApplyYay: Yay! Now we know the formula for the area of a sector.
en.s3ApplySolve: Let’s use it to solve some problems!
en.s3CentralIs: The angle between the two radii, at the centre, is called the central angle (θ) of the minor sector.
en.s3Central360Q: What happens when the central angle is 360°?
en.s3CentralFull: When θ = 360°, the two radii meet again, and the sector becomes the whole circle.
en.s3CentralWhole: So, the area of this sector is the area of the whole circle.
en.s3AreaAsk: Tap the formula for its area.
en.s3AreaWrongR: For area, the radius is squared: r².
en.s3AreaWrong2PiR: 2πr is the circumference, not the area.
en.s3AreaWrongD: Use the radius (r), not the diameter (d).
en.s3DeriveCut: We can cut the circle into 360 equal sectors of 1° each.
en.s3DeriveTogether: Together, these 360 sectors make the whole circle.
en.s3DeriveOne: So, one 1° sector is πr² divided by 360.
en.s3DeriveZoom: Let’s zoom in to see how small 1° is.
en.s3DeriveTen: A 10° sector is made of 10 such sectors.
en.s3DeriveMore: Let’s try a few more angles.
en.s3DeriveOnlyTop: Only the angle on top changes. 360 and πr² stay the same.
en.s3DeriveAskTheta: So, what is the area of a sector of angle θ?
en.s3DeriveRight: This is the formula for the area of a sector.
en.s3DeriveWrong2PiR: 2πr is the circumference. For area, use πr².
en.s3DeriveWrong180: A full turn is 360°, not 180°. So, divide θ by 360.
en.s3DeriveDrag: Drag the pink point to try any angle.
en.s3DeriveWorks: See? The formula works for every angle.
en.s3WkFind: Let’s find the area of this sector.
en.s3WkPutTheta: Now, put θ = 60° in the formula.
en.s3WkThetaRight: The sector is 60/360 of the whole circle.
en.s3WkThetaWrongFlip: Write the central angle on top and 360 at the bottom.
en.s3WkPutR: Now, put r = 21 cm in the formula. We take π = 22/7.
en.s3WkRWrong21: r² means r × r. So it is 21 × 21, or 21².
en.s3WkRWrongDouble: 2 × 21 is double the radius, not the square of the radius.
en.s3WkRWrong42: 42 cm is the diameter. Square the radius, which is 21 cm.
en.s3WkWrongWhole: That is the whole circle. Multiply by 1/6.
en.s3WkWrongThird: That is a third of the circle. 60° is 1/6 of 360°.
en.s3WkWrongHalf: That is half the circle. 60° is 1/6 of 360°.
en.s3WkFound: So, the area of the sector is 231 cm².
en.s3MinorAsk: Find the area of the minor sector.
en.s3P1WrongWhole: 2464 cm² is the area of the whole circle. A 90° sector is only 90/360 of it.
en.s3P1WrongR14: The radius is 28 cm. 154 cm² comes from using 14 cm.
en.s3P1Found: So, the area of the minor sector is 616 cm².
en.s3CmpAsk: Which minor sector has the greater area?
en.s3CmpRule: Use A = (θ/360) × πr² for each. For Circle II, find r from d first.
en.s3CmpRight: That’s correct! Both sectors have the same area.
en.s3CmpWhy1: Circle I has twice the radius, so its circle is 4 times bigger.
en.s3CmpWhy2: Circle II’s angle is 4 times bigger, so the two sectors balance.
en.s3RefFullTurn: Together, the two central angles make a full turn, 360°.
en.s3RefAsk: What is the central angle of the major sector?
en.s3RefRight: The central angle of the major sector is 260°.
en.s3RefWrongAdd: The two central angles add up to 360°. So, subtract 100° from 360°.
en.s3RefReflex: An angle greater than 180° is called a reflex angle. So, 260° is a reflex angle.
en.s3RefGeneral: In general, the central angle of the major sector = 360° − θ.
en.s3MaAsk: Which angle do we use in the formula for the major sector?
en.s3MaWrong100: 100° is the central angle of the minor sector. Use the central angle of the major sector.
en.s3MaWrong360: 360° is the whole circle. Use only the major sector’s angle.
en.s3MaSo: So, the area of the major sector = ((360° − θ)/360) × πr². Let’s use it with real numbers.
en.s3FindMajor: Find the area of the major sector.
en.s3WmFirst: First, find the central angle of the major sector.
en.s3WmRight: The central angle of the major sector is 315°.
en.s3WmPutR: Now, put r = 14 cm in the formula. We take π = 22/7.
en.s3WmRWrong14: r² means r × r. So it is 14 × 14, or 14².
en.s3WmRWrong28: 28 cm is the diameter. Square the radius, which is 14 cm.
en.s3WmRWrong7: 7 cm is half the radius. Square the radius, which is 14 cm.
en.s3WmWrongMinor: That is the minor sector: 1/8 of 616.
en.s3WmWrongWhole: That is the whole circle. Multiply by 7/8.
en.s3WmWrongHalf: That is half the circle. 315° is 7/8 of 360°.
en.s3WmFound: So, the area of the major sector is 539 cm².
en.s3AwAskCircle: What is the area of the circle?
en.s3AwWrong28Pi: 28π is 2πr, the circumference. For area, use πr².
en.s3AwWrong784: 784 = 28². Square the radius (14 cm), not the diameter.
en.s3AwWrong4: Area = π × r × r = π × 14 × 14, not π × 4 × 14.
en.s3AwAskMinor: Now, what is the area of the minor sector?
en.s3AwWrong78: 7/8 is the major sector’s share. The minor sector’s share is 45/360 = 1/8.
en.s3AwWrong784Pi: The area of the circle is 196π cm², not 784π cm².
en.s3AwWrongBoth: Check both parts: the minor sector is 1/8 of the circle, and the circle is 196π cm².
en.s3MajorByDiff: Area of the major sector = Area of the circle − Area of the minor sector.
en.s3AwSame: We get the same answer: 539 cm²!
en.s3MrTwoWays: There are two ways to find the area of a major sector.
en.s3MrWay1: Way 1: Use its own central angle, (360° − θ).
en.s3MrWay2: Way 2: Subtract the area of the minor sector from the area of the circle.
en.s3P3Rule: Area of the major sector = ((360° − θ)/360) × πr².
en.s3P3Found: So, the area of the major sector is 924 cm².
en.s3P4Given: The area of the circle is 2464 cm² and the area of the minor sector is 616 cm².
en.s3P4Found: So, the area of the major sector is 1848 cm².
